pred_reasoning_trace: A 58‐year‐old man presented to the emergency department with a 24‐hour history of right iliac fossa pain, nausea, and diarrhea. His surgical history was notable for a laparoscopic appendectomy performed 8 months earlier; he had no other significant past medical history. On examination, he was febrile, and his hemodynamic and respiratory parameters were stable. Abdominal palpation elicited pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs. Laboratory studies showed a white‐blood‐cell count of 25,000 cells/mm3 with 85% neutrophils and a C‐reactive protein level of 180 mg/dL; all other laboratory values were within normal limits. An abdominal CT scan demonstrated a swollen and thickened tubular structure measuring 36 × 27 mm at the cecal pole, with a 25‐mm pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips.
